topic: Mastering the Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

outline.topic: Mastering the Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Coordinate Systems as Languages
sections.content: Define a basis as a 'coordinate system'. Just as a point (3, 2) in standard 2D space relies on units (1,0) and (0,1), changing the basis means changing the 'grid lines' of our world. Visualize this as switching from a square grid to a skewed grid.
sections.example: Imagine a cat sitting on a map. If you use a grid of meters, it's at (2, 3). If you use a grid of 'cat-steps', its position (2, 3) changes to (1, 1). The cat didn't move; our language for describing its position did.

sections.title: Defining the Transition Matrix
sections.content: Introduce the Change of Basis Matrix (P). P is constructed by taking the vectors of the 'New Basis' (B') and expressing them in terms of the 'Old Basis' (B). Mathematically, [v]_B = P * [v]_B'.
sections.example: Visualize two sets of arrows. Set A (standard) and Set B (new, longer, rotated arrows). Draw P as the bridge that takes the coordinates from the Set B world and maps them back to the Set A world.

sections.title: The Mechanism: How to Calculate
sections.content: Break down the algorithm: 1. Identify Basis B and B'. 2. Write B' vectors as columns of P. 3. Multiply P by your coordinate vector to 'translate' your point into the standard basis.
sections.example: A robot arm needs to pick up a toy. The internal sensor uses 'Robot-Basis'. The table uses 'World-Basis'. By multiplying the Robot-Basis vector by P, the robot calculates the correct coordinates to reach the toy in the World-Basis.

sections.title: Summary & Geometric Intuition
sections.content: Reiterate that a change of basis is a 'relabelling' of space. The vector remains the same; only its representation in the column vector format changes. Emphasize that P^-1 allows you to go in reverse (from Standard to New Basis).
sections.example: Show a side-by-side animation: On the left, a point stays fixed while the coordinate axes rotate. On the right, the coordinate values (x, y) update in real-time as the axes transform.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: Coordinate Systems as Languages
lecture_lines: Basis vectors form our coordinate language.
Changing basis changes the grid lines.
Positions are defined by relative basis units.

lecture_lines: Columns of P are new basis vectors.

3. Show projection of v_A onto B basis in #00FF00 (green).

Step 3: Multiply P by coordinate vector.

storyboard.title: Summary & Geometric Intuition
lecture_lines: Change of basis is space relabelling.
The vector itself stays the same.
P-inverse converts back to original basis.
animations: 1. Show superposition of original and transformed grids in #FFFFFF.
2. Highlight vector v_A as stationary in #FFFF00.
3. Illustrate v_B as the result of M * v_A in #00FF00.
